newsitem.title: UK: Gengold seeks 353-working day year for gold mines.
newsitem.headline: Gengold seeks 353-working day year for gold mines.

text.p: Gengold, the South African mining division of Gencor Ltd, is aiming to agree a 353-day working year with the National Union of Minworkers (NUM), managing director Tom Dale told security analysts on Tuesday.
"The core issue is to get the mines working 353 days a year," he said.
Gengold was willing to table an offer intended to get Saturday and Sunday working in a 353-day production year.

Negotiations between the NUM and the employers' body, the Chamber of Mines, are under way on the 1997 wage and conditions and Dale told a questioner he was "totally dissatisfied" with having the Chamber negotiate on his behalf.
"If you want to improve productivity you have to pay people. Giving people inflation-related pay increases just to turn up at work is not going to help," he said.
"You need to have a large part of (the miner's) wage at risk. We put a scheme on the table last year which the Gengold workers wanted to take but could not do so due to central bargaining."
He said the Chamber of Mines had tabled an offer aimed at covering the union's core demands.
Gengold employs about 14,000 NUM members at its four South African gold mining properties.
In the March quarter the mines marginally increased gold output to 10,600 kilograms at a reduced working cost of rand 41,640 per kg from R41,728 per kg in the previous quarter.
The gold price received, however, fell nine percent to R51,210 per kg dropping gold revenue to R525.5 million from R557 million in the December quarter.

The Beatrix Mine's hedge which was put in place last year to finance the mine's No 6 shaft expansion realised slightly higher than the average price at R523,507 during the quarter and was placed to achieve about R53,000 in the June quarter.
"Productivity increases will raise output but we need more shifts to impact the bottom line. More shifts are imperative short term," he said.
